name: Research planning and roadmap
implementation_pattern: GitHub Project with a 'Research phase' single-select field and an iteration field; roadmap view for the timeline; one milestone per phase; sub-issues to break phases into tasks; a pinned roadmap issue.
evidence_note: STRICT rubric: capped at Limited because the support is a mandatory convention layered on a generic feature. Assembled from a generic project tool by convention; there is no 'research plan' object, the roadmap view has no dependencies, and Project field history is not meaningfully versioned.
residual_gap: Plan rationale and plan-revision history are weak.

name: Research question management
implementation_pattern: Register each research question as a dedicated issue (or an org Issue Type 'Question'), label it, and cross-reference the methods, analyses and outputs that address it; track reformulation in the issue timeline.
evidence_note: No research-question concept exists; the pattern is entirely convention on issues plus manual cross-referencing; discoverability is poor and question-to-artifact links are neither structured nor enforced.
residual_gap: No structured research-question model; evolution captured only as free-text timeline.

name: Task management
implementation_pattern: Issues as tasks with assignees, labels and sub-issues; a Project board with Status and Priority fields and built-in workflows; milestones for phase grouping; closing keywords bind completion to the change that resolved it.
evidence_note: Core task management is native and mature — GitHub's home ground.
residual_gap: No true dependency graph (only sub-issues and free-text 'blocked by').

name: Documentation
implementation_pattern: Version-controlled Markdown in the repo: a README per folder, methodology / protocol / decision-log documents, Mermaid diagrams; GitHub Pages for a rendered site; commit-pinned permalinks for precise references.
evidence_note: Version-controlled documentation created from project start is exactly what Markdown-in-repo provides.
residual_gap: No reference management or rich layout; requires Markdown literacy.

name: Decision traceability
implementation_pattern: A decision-record issue template (or a versioned DECISION_LOG.md) capturing rationale, alternatives, participants and date; discussion threads with mark-as-answer for deliberation; cross-references to the affected artifacts.
evidence_note: STRICT rubric: capped at Limited because the support is a mandatory convention layered on a generic feature. Workable and demonstrated by this repository, but GitHub does not distinguish research decisions from ordinary discussion; it depends entirely on a disciplined structured convention.
residual_gap: No native decision model; tacit decisions go unrecorded.

name: Collaboration and contribution tracking
implementation_pattern: Feature branches and pull requests with formal reviews, suggested changes and (optionally) required reviews / CODEOWNERS; forks for external contributors; co-authored-by for shared credit; Insights for the contribution overview.
evidence_note: Review, feedback, attribution and parallel work are all native.
residual_gap: Review-by-diff suits text and code better than some artifacts; enforcement is paid on private repos.

name: Communication
implementation_pattern: Discussions (categorised, searchable) for open questions and planning; issue comments for activity-bound conversation; @mentions and cross-references to link a thread to its tasks and artifacts.
evidence_note: Threaded, persistent, searchable, linkable communication is native.
residual_gap: Informal channels (email, chat) leak outside the system; topic-to-activity linking is manual.

name: Version control
implementation_pattern: Git for all text and code artifacts; tags and releases for named snapshots; the compare view for divergence; Git LFS for mid-size binaries.
evidence_note: History, diff, restore and snapshots are the platform substrate.
external_tools_needed: external data repository for large datasets
residual_gap: Large / binary data: LFS has quotas and no meaningful diff; large datasets belong elsewhere.

name: Research artifact management and integration
implementation_pattern: A defined repository structure (data/, analysis/, framework/, manuscript/ ...); README data dictionaries; labels for artifact classification; cross-references to artifacts held in external systems; a repository template to standardise the layout.
evidence_note: GitHub organises what it contains well, but the RE09 challenge — continuity across heterogeneous tools — is met only by reference, not containment.
external_tools_needed: external stores for large data and specialised-tool artifacts
residual_gap: Artifacts outside the repo are linked, not integrated; no unified index across tools.

name: Research provenance and artifact linkage
implementation_pattern: Reference every step: research-question issue -> method document -> data commit -> analysis PR -> result -> release; use closing keywords and PR 'linked issues'; the timeline and autogenerated release notes assemble the chain.
evidence_note: STRICT rubric: capped at Limited because the support is a mandatory convention layered on a generic feature. The connective tissue exists but is entirely manual, has no lineage query, and (per the literature) tends to stop at data and computation; upstream links depend on RM2 / RM5 discipline.
residual_gap: No automated lineage retrieval; no PROV / RO-Crate export; completeness depends on contributor discipline.

name: Transparency
implementation_pattern: A public (or shared) repository: visible Project status and issue / PR history, accessible Markdown documentation, a readable activity log and Insights; GitHub Pages for a public-facing summary.
evidence_note: A public GitHub repository is inherently transparent across status, history and documentation.
residual_gap: Embargoed material must be withheld; private repos limit third-party inspection.

name: Reproducibility support
implementation_pattern: Pin code and data versions with commits and tags; a GitHub Actions workflow that re-runs the analysis on a pinned environment (matrix across versions); Dependabot to record dependency changes; a PR checklist ('results reproduced? data documented?').
evidence_note: Supports the documentation and preservation side of reproducibility; environment capture and archival require external tooling, consistent with the requirement's 'support, not guarantee' scope.
external_tools_needed: containerisation (Docker / conda) for environments; Zenodo / repository for archival
residual_gap: No native environment capture; full re-execution guarantees are out of platform scope.

name: Automation
implementation_pattern: GitHub Actions workflows on push / PR / schedule / dispatch: validation and tests, documentation and figure regeneration, link checks, release packaging; job summaries and artifacts capture results; reusable workflows standardise across projects.
evidence_note: Event-, schedule- and dispatch-triggered automation is fully native.
residual_gap: High setup complexity; minutes quota; benefit concentrated in computational research.

name: Research output management and identification
implementation_pattern: Tag and cut a GitHub Release per research version with autogenerated notes and attached assets; a CITATION.cff file; enable the GitHub-Zenodo webhook so each release is archived and assigned a DOI.
evidence_note: Versioned, notes-bearing releases linked to the work since the last tag are native; persistent identifiers and long-term preservation are not — the standard GitHub-Zenodo integration (GC61) closes that gap and is the bridge to the prior reproducibility workflow.
external_tools_needed: Zenodo or an institutional repository for DOIs and preservation
residual_gap: Natively no persistent identifier and no archival guarantee; release assets are size-limited and non-archival.

name: Governance and sustainability
implementation_pattern: Repository roles and team-based permissions; visibility control; CONTRIBUTING and community-health files; CODEOWNERS for responsibility; the organisation audit log; a documented archival-exit route via Zenodo / export.
evidence_note: Access control and contribution guidelines are handled well, but governance and sustainability as a whole — ownership continuity, funding, workforce, institutional stewardship — are largely not platform matters, and the requirement is already flagged as only partly in scope.
external_tools_needed: institutional governance; external archive for exit
residual_gap: Most of the requirement (sustainability, funding, workforce) is outside any platform.
